headline: Web platforms unify transcriptomic, proteomic, imaging and genome annotation resources
label: Integrated Genomic Analysis Platforms
summary: Public imaging archives now exceed 11 PB, and genome browser releases add live configuration and streaming access for integrated analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is delivery of heterogeneous biological data through interactive or streamed interfaces. iGEX combines public and user-supplied transcriptomic and proteomic datasets for visual comparison of gene and protein expression. The BioImage Archive, holding over 11 PB of imaging data, offers OME-Zarr streaming access to its deposited records. The UCSC Genome Browser 2027 update adds QuickLift assembly annotation copying, HubSpace live configuration editing, custom display options, and 28 new tracks. The BioImage Archive is a deposition database rather than an analysis environment, so the shared thread is accessibility at the interface layer rather than analytic integration. What is new is the combination of user-supplied and public data in one view, petabyte-scale imaging accessed through streaming, and user-editable live annotation configuration.
